data.content_ref: inline:The preference for corroborated theories (SRC_001) inherits its normative force from an evolutionary selection mechanism (SRC_003); the 'decision' to prefer is not a voluntary convention but a methodological trait that survived because it correlates with truth-likeness. REFUTED IF: The history of science shows that methodological rules promoting corroboration have frequently led to the retention of false theories while eliminating true ones (i.e., if the selection pressure is orthogonal to verisimilitude).
